chains.title: One captured password-reset link becomes permanent ownership of a TOTP-protected account, including its recovery address
An account from the public registration form widens the workspace's TOTP window and lockouts, then guesses into a TOTP-protected administrator
An unauthenticated outsider eavesdrops on support conversations, becomes a chosen customer, and has the workspace mail that customer's conversation to the attacker
A delegated help-desk role enumerates and demotes the workspace's administrators, then breaks the authentication policy nobody is left to repair
An identity-provider account takes over an administrator past an enrolled second factor, and deactivating that administrator does not take the access away
An ordinary account builds a room the workspace joins every new employee to, and speaks in it with the server's own voice
A room ban removes nobody: the banned member keeps reading the room and returns through an invite its owners cannot revoke
Deleting a message deletes nothing: an outsider learns what was deleted, a member reads the text back, and an unauthenticated caller reads it too
